relationships.subject: O-1966
relationships.evidence_quote: When O-1966 was administered prior to or simultaneous with morphine, morphine antinociception was attenuated and antinociceptive tolerance was exacerbated.

relationships.subject: O-1966
relationships.evidence_quote: Administration of O-1966 prior to each morphine injection during the chronic dosing regimen led to a significantly more pronounced tolerance than did morphine alone.

relationships.subject: O-1966
relationships.evidence_quote: When O-1966 was administered following morphine, morphine antinociception was not affected and antinociceptive tolerance was attenuated.

relationships.subject: O-1966
relationships.evidence_quote: O-1966 alone at the 10 μM concentration attenuates morphine-stimulated [35S]GTPγS binding, and that this attenuation is blocked by co-administration of SR144528

relationships.subject: SR144528
relationships.evidence_quote: Pretreatment with CB2 antagonist at the same dose as CB2 agonist showed that SR144528 attenuated the sub-additive interaction and restored the morphine dose-effect curve.

key_findings: The CB2 agonist O-1966 attenuates acute morphine antinociception and worsens tolerance when given before or with morphine, but attenuates tolerance and hyperalgesia when given after morphine.
O-1966 reduced morphine-stimulated GTPgammaS binding at the mu-opioid receptor in CB2-free cells, suggesting direct negative allosteric modulation.
